case_name: Jaipur Development Authority v Ram Sahai and Another
respondent:
Ram Sahai and Another
Supreme Court of India

31 October 2006
Appeal (civil) 4626 of 2006, S.L.P. (C) No. 23715 of 2004
The Judgment was delivered by : S .B. Sinha, J.
Leave granted.
1. Appellant herein is a State within the meaning of Article 12 of the Constitution of India. It is created under the Jaipur Development Authority Act. Respondent was appointed on daily-wage basis from September, 1986 to June, 1987. His services were dispensed with, with effect from 01 July 1987. He raised an industrial dispute and on receipt of failure report dated 26 April 1988 of the Conciliation Officer, the Government of Rajasthan made a reference for adjudication of the following dispute to the Presiding Officer, Labour Court at Jaipur, in exercise of its power under Section 10(1)(c) of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 :
"Whether termination of service of workman Shri Ramsahai s/o Chhotu through Shri M.F. Beg Labour Welfare Centre, near Mayank Cinema, Station Road, Jai
facts: The appellant is a State within the meaning of Article 12 of the Constitution of India.
Respondent was appointed on daily-wage basis from September, 1986 to June, 1987.
His services were dispensed with, with effect from 01 July 1987.

He raised an industrial dispute and on receipt of failure report dated 26 April 1988 of the Conciliation Officer, the Government of Rajasthan made a reference for adjudication of the following dispute to the Presiding Officer, Labour Court at Jaipur...
The Labour Court in its Award, inter alia, held that the respondent has not been in continuous service for a period of 240 days with twelve months immediately preceding his termination.
It was further held that the plea of the appellant herein that he had abandoned his services is not correct.

Mr. S.K. Bhattacharya, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant would contend that the recruitment and termination of Respondent being on daily-wage basis, Sections 25G and 25H of the Act have no application in the instant case.
issues: Whether termination of service of workman Shri Ramsahai s/o Chhotu through Shri M.F. Beg Labour Welfare Centre, near Mayank Cinema, Station Road, Jaipur w.e.f. 01 July 87 by the Secretary, Jaipur Development Authority, Jaipur and the Garden Specialist, Jaipur Development Authority, Jaipur is reasonable and legal.
petitioner_arguments: The recruitment and termination of Respondent being on daily-wage basis, Sections 25G and 25H of the Act have no application in the instant case.
The workman having voluntarily abandoned his services, the Labour Court wrongly opined that he was retrenched from service.
respondent_arguments: Sections 25G and 25H of the Act stand on a different footing, vis-'-vis, 25F thereof, in so far as, for the purpose of invoking the said provisions, it is not necessary that the workman must complete a continuous service of 240 days within a period of twelve calendar months preceding the order of termination as envisaged under Section 25B of the Act.
court_reasoning: The statute does not envisage application of the provisions of the Act and Rule where both recruitment and termination is uncertain or when the workmen are not required to be recruited in a category-wise service, e.g., skilled, semi-skilled or unskilled, etc.

Labour Court may be correct in arriving at the conclusion that there was nothing to show that the provisions of Sections 25G and 25H had been complied, but there is also no finding as to whether in a situation of this nature the same were required to be complied with.
holding: The termination of workman Ramsahai son of Shri Chhotu Ram by the respondents w.e.f. 01 July 87 is not reasonable and legal.
He is reinstated back in service.

His continuity in service is maintained, and from the date of his termination till the date of award he is awarded all back wages along with other benefits which he would have received while in continuous service and from the date of award the workman shall receive the wages and other benefits which other similarly situated workmen junior to him are receiving today.
